data.name: Vanna
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Vanna was the goddess of fertility, birth, and the weaving loom. She was also known as the protector of women in childbirth. In Christianity, Vanna can be seen as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who brought new life into the world through her son, Jesus.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the divine feminine and the power of creation.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vanna, with its roots in Greek mythology, carries a rich cultural heritage as the goddess of fertility, birth, and weaving. It represents the powerful and essential role of women in the creation of new life and the weaving of the fabric of society.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Vanna can be seen as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who brought new life into the world through her son, Jesus, and continued to nurture and protect humanity as a devoted and loving mother. Vanna represents the divine feminine, and the strength and grace embodied in the Blessed Mother, whom Christians look to for intercession, guidance, and inspiration.
